free_tier.stated: Welcome credit: USD 1, added once your email is confirmed and your card is saved; machines cannot be started without a card on file with auto-refill.
free_tier.notes: The USD 1 is a one-time welcome credit, not a recurring allowance, and it is gated on both email confirmation and a saved card. A card on file with auto-refill is required to start any machine; without a card, creating or starting a machine returns 402.

per_object_cap.stated: Not applicable: the unit is a machine, not an object. Machine sizes are tiny (0.5 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 8 GB disk), small (1 vCPU, 6 GB, 12 GB), medium (2 vCPU, 8 GB, 16 GB) and large (4 vCPU, 12 GB, 20 GB).

retention.stated: A stopped machine keeps its entire filesystem snapshot, installed apps, browser profiles with cookies, and open windows and tabs until the user destroys it; stopped (snapshot) machines cost USD 0.001 per hour.

egress.terms: A VPN add-on is priced separately: Proxy at +USD 0.03/h and USD 10/GB, Unlock at +USD 0.06/h and USD 15/GB and USD 3 per 1k connections; no base egress allowance is stated on the billing page.

interface_detail: An MCP endpoint per machine plus a REST API (POST /api/machines, GET /api/machines/{id}/screenshot.jpg) and a dashboard; bearer tokens are API keys (tmk_), machine tokens (tmm_) or OAuth tokens (tmo_).
tooling: Any MCP client, including Claude Code and Cursor, connects over HTTP to a machine's MCP URL; a REST API and a web dashboard also drive machines.
chaining: A machine's persistent browser logins and credential vault survive stop/start, so a long agent task can resume signed in; a per-machine token can be handed to a customer's agent while the platform key stays on the operator's server.

limits.value: USD 1 one-time welcome credit, only after email confirmation and a saved card
Without a card, creating or starting a machine returns 402; auto-refill charges the card when the balance falls below a chosen threshold (default USD 5) by a set amount (default USD 20)

limits_note: Running machines are stopped when the balance reaches zero and their state is kept; admin accounts do not need a card.
binding_note: The card on file with auto-refill is the first gate: no card means no machine can start at all, even with welcome credit, and the credit itself is conditioned on the card being saved.

identity_cost.detail: Registration posts email, password and name (POST /api/auth/register) and sends a confirmation email; the billing page states the welcome credit is added once the email is confirmed and a card is saved, and that starting machines requires a card on file with auto-refill. No phone or ID document is stated.

reliability_note: A running machine with an empty balance is stopped and keeps its state; the whole disk is snapshotted on stop and a save point is taken every 30 minutes while running, so at most 30 minutes of change can be lost on a crash.
confidence_note: Prices, credit, card gate and machine sizes are quoted from the vendor's billing, machines and authentication docs read on 2026-11-25; identity fields are from the registration API description on the same site.

notes: A persistent Linux desktop machine with a signed-in browser and credential vault, not a short-lived ephemeral sandbox. Price at the 2 vCPU/8 GB medium size is USD 0.16 per running hour, billed by the minute; a stopped snapshot is USD 0.001 per hour. The USD 1 welcome credit is a one-time credit gated on email confirmation and a saved card, and a card with auto-refill is required before any machine can start. The list price at 2 vCPU/4 GB would be USD 0.11/h on the small size, but the small has 1 vCPU/6 GB, so no 2 vCPU/4 GB shape is sold here.
